_metadata.title: Cluevoyance Unlimited - 20-word pair-clue pilot
_metadata.clue_text_rule: One uppercase word, or a familiar two-word phrase, up to 18 characters including the space. The game does not enforce a length in code (EditableClueTab only trims and uppercases). A clue may never be one of the twenty pilot words: a board word used as a clue is unplayable.
_metadata.quality_note: Every clue here survived the hand audit recorded in pilot-clue-quality-audit.json. That audit is editorial judgement, not something the validator can prove; validate-pilot.mjs checks structure only.

clues.explanation: A bridge spans the river from one bank to the other.
You cross a bridge to reach the far bank.
A canal has banks on both sides and a bridge over it every mile.
The crown is royalty and Royal Bank is one of the commonest bank names there is.
The Royal Mint belongs to the crown and strikes the coins the banks hand out.
A sovereign is the crowned head of state and also the gold coin a bank once paid out.
Diamonds are kept in a bank vault.
The diamond heist and the bank job are the same film plot.
A diamond goes in a safe and the safe goes in a bank.
A plane banks into a turn on the power of its engines.
A plane banks into a turn, and an engine turns over when it starts.
A bank has a drive-through window and an engine is the thing that drives.
A fire alarm and a bank alarm are both standard emergency fixtures.
A firebreak stops a blaze spreading, and to break the bank means to spend everything.
Banks keep valuables in safes, and those safes are specifically built to be fireproof.
A bank vault holds the money and a burial vault holds the dead.
A bank account is the everyday one; a ghost account is the dormant or fake one nobody is behind.
A ghost town with its abandoned bank and open vault is the stock Western image.
A blood bank stores the blood the heart pumps.

A trust is a banking arrangement and trust is a matter of the heart.
Bees store honey for the winter exactly as a bank stores money.
Robbing a bank is the classic crime, and robbing the hive is the beekeeper's own word for taking the honey.

A horse charges into battle and bank charges are the fees on your account.
You bet on a horse and you bank on a sure thing; both are staking money on an outcome.
Banks hold gold bars and iron bars are what keep a vault shut.

A bank safe is a box of thick iron.
A bank vault is the thing a key is needed for.
A safe deposit box sits in a bank and opens with the customer's own key.
A bank locks its money away and a key is what opens a lock.

A streetlight stands on it and a high-street bank stands on it too.
A green light means go and greenbacks are the money a bank holds.
You check your hair in the mirror and you write a check on the bank.
A mirror is silvered glass and silver is the metal banking was built on.
Banks have a night deposit box, and night is when the moon is out.
A river runs between its banks and Moon River is the song everyone knows.
A rose bed is where they are planted and a river bed sits between the banks.
A rose bursts into bloom and a river bursts its banks.
A hedge fund is a bank's business and the wild rose is the hedgerow flower.
A salt deposit is laid down underground and a bank deposit is paid in over the counter.
Worth your salt is the idiom and net worth is the figure the bank cares about.

A shady bank is where you sit on a hot day, and a shady bank is also a crooked one.
A cloud bank is a real formation and a passing cloud is what drags a shadow across the ground.
A river snakes across the country between its two banks.

Spring break is the holiday and breaking the bank is the idiom for overspending.
A spring is where water comes out of the ground and a bank is what water runs between.
A crown and a bridge are both things a dentist fits in your mouth.
A crown caps one tooth and a bridge spans the gap where others are missing.
An arch is what holds a stone bridge up, and the crown is the architect's name for the very top of it.
Diamonds is a card suit and bridge is a card game.

Both belong to the same deck of fifty-two.
A ship has a bridge where the captain stands and an engine room below decks.
A railway bridge is built for the engine to cross.
Iron bridges and steam engines were both held together with rivets.
To burn your bridges is the idiom, and burning is what fire does.
Crossfire is what you get caught in and crossing is what a bridge is for.
London Bridge is the one in the nursery rhyme and the Great Fire of London is the city's other famous story.
A toll is what you pay to cross a bridge and a bell tolls for the dead.
Crossing over is the gentle word for dying, and crossing over is what you do on a bridge.
The other side is the afterlife, and it is also simply the far end of the bridge.
Hearts is a card suit and bridge is a card game.
Cross my heart is the promise and crossing is what a bridge is for.
A bridge closes a gap and a hole in the heart is a gap surgeons close.
Winnie-the-Pooh wants honey above everything, and Poohsticks is the game you play from a bridge.
Honey is what a sweet tooth wants and a bridge is what the dentist fits once the teeth have gone.

A bridge is built out of iron girders.

The troll lives under the bridge in its shadow.

A bridge arch throws a black shadow on the water below.
A river snakes across the country and a bridge is what gets you over it.
The cables slung across a suspension bridge hang in long snaking curves.

A bridge crosses water and a spring is where that water starts.

Egyptian pharaohs wore a rearing cobra on the front of the crown.

A cobra's hood flares out around its head exactly where a crown would sit.
A flower crown is what is worn at spring festivals.
The May Queen is crowned to mark the arrival of spring.
The crown of a tree is its top, and in spring that crown comes into leaf.

A diamond is pure carbon, and carbon is what burns in a fire.

A diamond ring is what you offer along with your heart.
Honey crystallises in the jar and a diamond is a crystal that never will.

A horse races and an engine races when it runs away with itself.

An engine block is cast iron.

A ship's engine spends its life fighting salt air.

A snake hisses and so does an engine letting off steam or air.

The hoses coiled under a car bonnet look exactly like snakes.
An engine's valves are held shut by valve springs.
An engine fires through its ignition coil and a spring is a coil of wire.
Clockwork is an engine driven entirely by a wound spring.
